Use it in your terminal, IDE, or tag @claude on Github. **Learn more in the [official documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview)**. ## Get started > [!NOTE] > Installation via npm is deprecated. Use one of the recommended methods below. For more installation options, uninstall steps, and troubleshooting, see the [setup documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup). 1. Install Claude Code: **MacOS/Linux (Recommended):** ```bash curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ``` **Homebrew (MacOS/Linux):** ```bash brew install --cask claude-code ``` **Windows (Recommended):** ```powershell irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` **WinGet (Windows):** ```powershell winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode ``` **NPM (Deprecated):** ```bash npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code ``` 2. Navigate to your project directory and run `claude`. ## Plugins Anthropic's Claude Code plugins are developed in [claude-plugins-official](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official). See the [plugins directory](./plugins/README.md) for more about plugins. ## Reporting Bugs We welcome your feedback. Use the `/bug` command to report issues directly within Claude Code, or file a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues). ## Connect on Discord Join the [Claude Developers Discord](https://anthropic.com/discord) to connect with other developers using Claude Code. Get help, share feedback, and discuss your projects with the community. ## Data collection, usage, and retention When you use Claude Code, we collect feedback, which includes usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the `/bug` command. ### How we use your data See our [data usage policies](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage). ### Privacy safeguards We have implemented several safeguards to protect your data, including limited retention periods for sensitive information, restricted access to user session data, and clear policies against using feedback for model training. readmeHtml:
Claude Code

Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, and handling git workflows -- all through natural language commands. Use it in your terminal, IDE, or tag @claude on Github.

Learn more in the official documentation.

Get started

Note

Installation via npm is deprecated. Use one of the recommended methods below.

For more installation options, uninstall steps, and troubleshooting, see the setup documentation.

  1. Install Claude Code:

    MacOS/Linux (Recommended):

    curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

    Homebrew (MacOS/Linux):

    brew install --cask claude-code

    Windows (Recommended):

    irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

    WinGet (Windows):

    winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode

    NPM (Deprecated):

    npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

  2. Navigate to your project directory and run claude.

Plugins

Anthropic's Claude Code plugins are developed in claude-plugins-official. See the plugins directory for more about plugins.

Reporting Bugs

We welcome your feedback. Use the /bug command to report issues directly within Claude Code, or file a GitHub issue.

Connect on Discord

Join the Claude Developers Discord to connect with other developers using Claude Code. Get help, share feedback, and discuss your projects with the community.

Data collection, usage, and retention

When you use Claude Code, we collect feedback, which includes usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the /bug command.

How we use your data

See our data usage policies.

Privacy safeguards

We have implemented several safeguards to protect your data, including limited retention periods for sensitive information, restricted access to user session data, and clear policies against using feedback for model training.

For full details, please review our Commercial Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

releases.name: v2.1.331
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added Code Mode support in terminal sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS
- Added `oidc.groups_jsonpath` to the Claude apps gateway, to read groups from the matching entries of a list of objects with a small subset of JSONPath (RFC 9535)
- Added an API connectivity section to `claude doctor` that reports whether the API can be reached, with the HTTP status or the error, or says why it wasn't tested
- Added a notice when tap-mode voice dictation stops by itself, after 15 seconds without recognized speech or at its 2-minute limit
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_RESPONSE_COMPRESSION` to ask for uncompressed model responses behind a proxy that cuts compressed ones off; not advised yet for self-hosted runners or Remote Control
- Added `CLAUDE_GATEWAY_IDP_CONNECT_BY_HOSTNAME=1` for Claude apps gateways: with `oidc.use_proxy: true`, sign-in requests hand the proxy an `https` IdP's hostname even with `NO_PROXY` set

releases.name: v2.1.330
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added sign-in to organizations managed in Anthropic's Enterprise Admin Console: after `claude auth login`, Claude Code applies the organization's settings and uses its cloud provider or gateway
- Added easel, a built-in mod that draws charts when asked and under MCP metrics results, on Pro, Max and, where available, Team and Enterprise on macOS and Linux; turn automatic charts off in `/config`
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_FULL_SIGN_IN_LINK=1` to print the full sign-in link, if the short one shows an error or a script reads values from it
- Self-hosted runner: Added `--start-dir` / `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_START_DIR` to have Claude start its work in a folder of a repository, while settings and hooks load as without it
- Added a notice in cloud and self-hosted runner sessions when a plugin marketplace can't be fetched because its repository isn't one of the session's
- Self-hosted runner: Added a notice when Anthropic-managed git refuses a plugin's own repository, naming the plugin and what to do
- Added `commandPrinted` to `claude plugin install --json` results, true when the plugin's install command wrote to stderr, and `commandFailed` when it exited with an error, was kill

releases.name: v2.1.329
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added a trust dialog warning that says where a folder's hooks are declared
- Added a warning in the conversation, in Claude Desktop and other non-interactive hosts, when hooks in managed settings fail to load
- Added this session's scheduled tasks, `/loop` wakeups, the goal and this conversation's forks to `/tasks`; x stops one after asking
- Added a "Server message" row to a server's page in `/mcp` that shows the JSON-RPC error message of a remote HTTP MCP server that refuses the connection
- Added a "Marketplace auto-update" row to `/status` that names managed marketplaces that get no automatic updates, and why
- Added support for turning on Code Mode while OpenTelemetry events and metrics are enabled; each tool call the code makes sends its events; tracing still keeps it off
- Fixed `~/.claude.json` sometimes being reset to defaults when a network stall or file lock made it unreadable and cleared during a save
- Fixed repeated sign-outs on macOS when Claude Code could read the Keychain but not save to it. That session now stops at expiry and says why, and other sessions stay signed in
- Fixed `/terminal-setup` corrupting VS Code settings or keybindings files

releases.name: v2.1.328
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added auto mode for Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude apps gateway; interactive sessions with no permission mode start in it
- Added `"onFailure": "block"` for `mcp_tool` hooks, as for command and HTTP hooks: a hook whose call fails blocks the action
- Added a warning when a message from a session that skips permission prompts may be held and dropped by a cloud session
- Added a notice in `/status` and `claude doctor` when an OpenTelemetry exporter has no endpoint and its data would likely be lost
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_DEFERRED_TOOL_RESUME`, which lets a host stop `claude -p --resume` and `--continue` from running a tool call that a hook deferred
- Added support for apps that embed Claude Code to switch on the policy plugin's `allowManagedModsOnly` option; an admin's managed settings still win
- Added a startup warning to the Claude apps gateway when a policy's `maxEffortLevel` is not a valid effort level

aiSummary.oneLiner: An official, terminal-based AI coding assistant powered directly by the Claude model family.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Claude Code is a command-line interface tool developed by Anthropic that deeply integrates their Claude AI models directly into a developer's local environment. It is designed to understand entire codebases by autonomously navigating directories, reading files, and executing local shell commands for context. The tool assists with complex refactoring, bug hunting, and feature implementation without requiring developers to leave their terminal or copy-paste code into a browser. It maintains a secure, local execution perimeter while leveraging the advanced reasoning capabilities of models like Claude 3.5 Sonnet. This drastically reduces context switching and accelerates the software development lifecycle.
keyFeatures: Native terminal integration: Operates entirely within the command line, integrating seamlessly into existing shell environments and workflows.
Autonomous codebase navigation: Capable of searching directories, reading files, and grepping for specific patterns to build context automatically.
Local command execution: Safely runs local tests, linters, and build scripts to verify code changes before finalizing them.
Advanced model reasoning: Powered directly by Anthropic's most capable models, ensuring high-quality architectural advice and code generation.
Context-aware refactoring: Understands the broader repository structure, allowing it to safely execute multi-file changes and updates.

useCases.title: Automated Bug Resolution
useCases.description: Instruct the assistant to locate the source of a specific error trace, write the fix, and run the test suite to verify it.

useCases.title: Complex Code Refactoring
useCases.description: Command the tool to migrate an entire directory of components to a new framework API across multiple interdependent files.

useCases.title: Codebase Onboarding
useCases.description: Ask the terminal assistant to explain the architecture and data flow of a massive, unfamiliar repository dynamically.

useCases.title: Rapid Feature Implementation
useCases.description: Describe a new feature in natural language and allow the tool to scaffold the necessary files, logic, and tests automatically.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Professional software engineers and developers who prefer working in terminal environments and want powerful, context-aware AI assistance. It requires familiarity with command-line interfaces and local development workflows.
